Becfhola.json.text: Becfhola is an Irish goddess or heroine. Her other names are Becfola and Beagfhola. She is a mortal queen of Tara. She is the central figure of the tale Tochmarc Becfhola, the Wooing of Becfhola. The tale tells of her affair with a fairy lover named Flann ua Fedach. As queen of Tara, Becfhola stands for the idea of Sovereignty. Her unhappiness with King Diarmait and her preference for the hero Crimthann may have cost Diarmait his right to rule. Becfhola planned a meeting with Crimthann on an island in Lough Erne. She met Flann instead and spent an enchanted night with him. She lived in fairy time while she was away. When she returned to Tara, no time appeared to have passed. Flann soon came to take her away.

Bedwyr.json.text: Bedwyr is a Welsh hero. His other names are Bedivere and Bedwyr fab Bedrawg. He appears in the Welsh tale of Kulhwch and Olwen, where he is a warrior of high standing. He is brave and never shies from a fight. He is handsome, though less so than the hero Arthur and far less than Lancelot. In later Arthurian stories his standing falls. Writers call him only Arthur's butler. Yet one remnant of his old importance survives. Bedwyr must throw the great sword Excalibur into the water. The Lady of the Lake then reclaims it. After that task, Bedwyr places the dying king in the boat that heads to Avalon.

Belatucadros.json.text: Belatucadros is a Continental Celtic god. His other name is Belatucadros. He is an obscure Gaulish deity. His name means beautiful in slaughter, or fair slayer. The Romans compared him with their war god Mars. He left many small dedications across northwestern England. This evidence shows that the lowly soldiers most favored his cult. He never appears with a female partner. His worship was simple and not elaborate.

Belenus.json.text: Belenus is a Continental Celtic god. His other names are Bel and Belinus. Knowledge of him is thin, but he was wide-ranging. Roman writers compared him to Apollo. People worshipped him at healing waters, including Aquae Borvonis at Bourbon-les-Bains in France. The healing plant Belinuntia takes his name. His name appears to mean 'bright one' or 'shining one'. For this reason he may be a solar and healing divinity. Some scholars say the spring festival Beltane took its name from him. Heriot wrote that is a conjecture. His cult left many inscriptions through Gaul. In later British legend, Geoffrey of Monmouth tells of a hero Belinus, twin brother of Brennius, who shares the true flesh of power.

Beli.json.text: Beli is a Celtic ancestral figure, and he is many also a god. His full title is Beli Mawr, or Beli Mawr fab Tacitus. He is a father in the Welsh family line and may descend from the god Bel onal Berea. In the Mabinogion he is the consort of the mother goddess Do the goddess Arianrhod and the warrior Casaccia. In the tale of Maxin, Beli rules Britain until the hero arrives with his armies and pushes him into the sea. Writers have cast him as a god of death and of the sea. The ocean is sometimes called 'Blook li' or the liquor of the sun. The London place named Billingsgate appears to hold his name. Some writers link him to a little-known Irish god called Bile.

Belisama.json.text: Belisama is a Continental Celtic and British goddess. Her other names are Belesama and Belisma. Unlike most deities, she is honored in several places. She is a cosmic goddess of the heavens and a goddess of rivers. Rivers shelter the sun's finest deities of fortune in the Celtic view. Her name derives from words for brightness, or shining. Some say she is the Continental kin of the Irish flame goddess Brigit. Identity: the Romans linked her to Minerva, the same way they linked the hot-spring goddess Sul of Bath. In Langthe ancient River Ribble carried her name. The headless woman's statue found near that river may represent her. The stream soon came to be called Peg O'Neill, a drowned serving girl who claims a victim every seven years.

Bellieus.json.text: Bellieus is an Arthurian hero. He is a knight of the Round TableHotel in the tales of King Arthur. He joins the Round Table in a curious way. He once finds the pure knight Lancelot in bed with his own lady. Lancelot claims the meeting is a pure mistake. Bellieus, bound by honor, must challenge the intruder. Lancelot is the better swordsman. Bellieus takes wounds in the duel but survives. After the fight he serves along the Red at Arthur's court of Camelot.

Beltane.json.text: Beltane is a Celtic festival. His other names are Bealtaine, Beltain, Beltine, May Eve, and May Day. It is celebrated on the first of May.May. It is one of the four great festivals of the old Irish seasonal year. Beltane is a farming festival. It marks the start of summer and the walk of cattle from winter pens to the green mountain pastures of the summer grass. The feast begins at the end on the eve. Like Samhain, the day opens the door to the fairy world and lets the dead and the living speak. But Samhain honors the dead and Beltane honors the living. The name draws up words for fire May. People at Beltane put out the hearth fires. They relight them from a bonfire lit on the nearest signal hill.

Beltany.json.text: Beltany is an Irish mythological site. It stands in the far northwest of County Donegal. A large circle of about sixty stones catches the beams of the rising sun on the morning of Beltane, the first of May. An alignment between a pillar stone and another stone carved with cup marks lines up with that sunrise. Most Irish stone circles with such alignments were built as much as four thousand years before the Celtic people arrived. Those earlier builders marked the equinoxes. Beltany is puzzling.
